stem: An internal microservice platform uses Application Load Balancers with hostnames under the private domain corp.internal. Security requires TLS on every ALB with certificates that renew automatically and are trusted only by company clients. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Buy certificates for the corp.internal names from a commercial public CA and store them in Secrets Manager with rotation enabled
Create self-signed certificates with OpenSSL, import them into ACM, and run a scheduled Lambda function that replaces them yearly
Create an AWS Private CA and issue private certificates through ACM for the corp.internal names so ACM renews them automatically
Request public certificates for the corp.internal names from ACM and validate them by adding CNAME records to a private hosted zone

stem: An audit found that some clients upload and download objects from a company S3 bucket over plain HTTP. The company must reject every request to the bucket that is not encrypted in transit, whatever IAM permissions the caller has. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Add a bucket policy statement that denies all S3 actions on the bucket when the aws:SecureTransport condition is false
Turn on S3 server access logging and use Amazon Athena to find callers that use HTTP so they can be contacted and fixed
Enable default encryption with SSE-KMS on the bucket so that all objects are encrypted with a customer managed key when stored
Enable S3 Block Public Access on the bucket so that anonymous HTTP requests are rejected before they reach the objects

stem: An IoT platform writes 50 million log objects per month to S3, each about 8 KB. Logs are never read after 7 days but must be kept for 5 years. A lifecycle rule that transitions each object to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days is costing more than expected. Which change lowers the total cost the MOST?

choices.text: Periodically combine the small logs into large compressed archive objects and apply the Deep Archive lifecycle rule only to those archives
Transition the individual objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval instead of Deep Archive so each transition request is billed at a lower rate
Transition the individual objects to S3 Standard-IA after 7 days and to Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days to spread transition charges
Move each log object into S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archive access tiers enabled so S3 moves the objects between tiers automatically

stem: A company stores 40 TB of project files on an Amazon EFS Standard file system mounted by EC2 instances in three Availability Zones. Analysis shows that about 85% of the files have not been opened in over 90 days, but any file may be needed again without notice. The file system must stay Multi-AZ. What is the MOST cost-effective change?

choices.text: Switch the file system from Elastic throughput to Provisioned throughput sized for the peak, so storage is billed at a lower rate
Replace the file system with EFS One Zone and turn on its automatic backups so that files can be restored after an AZ failure
Configure EFS lifecycle management to move unused files to Infrequent Access and then Archive, and back to Standard on access
Copy files not opened for 90 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive with DataSync and delete them from the file system afterwards

stem: A media company's upload service uses S3 multipart uploads for large video files. The bucket does not use versioning, and a listing of all objects shows about 3 TB, but the monthly bill charges for about 11 TB of S3 Standard storage in that bucket. What is the MOST likely cause and fix?

choices.text: Server access logs are being delivered into the same bucket; move log delivery to another bucket and delete the older log files
Deleted objects are kept as noncurrent versions; add a lifecycle rule that expires noncurrent object versions after a few days
S3 bills Standard storage at a 128 KB minimum per object; transition the smaller objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering right away
Failed and abandoned multipart uploads leave stored parts; add a lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days

stem: A CPU-bound image processing Lambda function written in Python runs 30 million times per month with 512 MB of memory and an average duration of 4 seconds. The code has no native x86-only dependencies. Which TWO changes are MOST likely to reduce the function's cost? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable provisioned concurrency for the peak concurrency level so that invocations avoid cold start charges
Test higher memory settings with a tool such as AWS Lambda Power Tuning and choose the one with the lowest cost
Reduce the memory setting to 128 MB, because Lambda bills only for memory size and not for invocation duration
Move the function into a VPC so that it can use private subnets and avoid Lambda request charges on invocations
Change the function architecture to arm64 so it runs on AWS Graviton processors at a lower price per GB-second

stem: A retailer needs 40 m7i.2xlarge instances guaranteed in one specific Availability Zone for a three-week sales event starting next month. After the event the instances will be terminated, and the company does not want any commitment that lasts beyond the event. Which option meets these needs MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Request 40 Spot Instances in that Availability Zone with the capacity-optimized strategy and a maximum price set high
Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation for the 40 instances in that Availability Zone with an end date after the event
Purchase 40 Regional Reserved Instances with a one-year term and sell them in the Reserved Instance Marketplace later
Purchase a one-year Compute Savings Plan that covers the hourly cost of the 40 instances for the event period

stem: A company's EC2 and Fargate usage across all accounts, priced at Compute Savings Plan rates, ranges from $40 per hour at night to $100 per hour at weekday peaks and has not dropped below $40 per hour in the past year. It wants to buy a Compute Savings Plan to lower costs without paying for unused commitment. Which commitment should it choose?

choices.text: About $100 per hour, the peak usage, so that every hour of compute is fully covered at the discounted Savings Plan rate
About $70 per hour, the daily average, so that unused commitment at night is balanced by extra coverage at peaks
About $40 per hour, the steady baseline, with usage above it billed at On-Demand rates or covered by Spot later
No commitment, and instead buy Standard Reserved Instances for the peak hours only, since RIs can be scheduled

stem: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster runs an I/O-heavy transaction workload. Cost Explorer shows that I/O request charges make up about 55% of the cluster's monthly Aurora bill, and the traffic will stay at this level. Which change reduces the database cost the MOST without changing the application?

choices.text: Add two Aurora Replicas and point read queries at the reader endpoint so the writer handles fewer I/O operations
Change the instances to a smaller class and add an ElastiCache cluster that caches every write before it reaches Aurora
Migrate the cluster to Aurora Serverless v2 so that compute scales down and I/O is billed only when queries run
Change the cluster storage configuration from Aurora Standard to Aurora I/O-Optimized so that I/O requests are not billed

stem: A DynamoDB table stores 30 TB of order history. Only orders from the last few weeks are read or updated regularly, and older items are read a few times a year for customer inquiries with the same single-digit millisecond latency. Storage now accounts for most of the table's cost. What is the MOST cost-effective change?

choices.text: Switch the table to the DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access table class, which lowers storage price for the same latency
Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the table so that reads of older order items are served from the cache
Export items older than 90 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a nightly job and delete them from the table afterwards
Switch the table from on-demand to provisioned capacity with auto scaling so that the storage portion of the bill falls

stem: An Amazon ECS cluster on Fargate runs in private subnets and pulls large container images from Amazon ECR many times a day. The NAT gateway's data processing charges have become the largest networking cost. Which TWO changes remove image pull traffic from the NAT gateway? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create an S3 gateway VPC endpoint and add it to the private subnets' route tables, because ECR stores image layers in S3
Add a second NAT gateway in each Availability Zone so each task uses the NAT gateway closest to it for image downloads
Move the tasks to public subnets with public IP addresses and keep the NAT gateway in place for all other outbound traffic
Create a VPC peering connection to the AWS account that hosts ECR so image pulls take a private path through the peering
Create interface VPC endpoints for ECR (ecr.api and ecr.dkr) in the VPC so the ECR API calls stay on private addresses

stem: Two EC2 instances in the same VPC and the same Availability Zone exchange about 50 TB of data per month. The bill shows unexpected data transfer charges for this traffic. The application is configured to reach its peer using the peer's Elastic IP address. What change removes these charges?

choices.text: Enable enhanced networking with ENA on both instances so that data transfer between them is billed at a lower rate
Replace the Elastic IP addresses with new auto-assigned public IP addresses, because Elastic IP traffic is billed at a premium
Configure the application to use the peer's private IP address or private DNS name so traffic stays on the private network
Place both instances in a cluster placement group so that traffic between them uses a faster network path within the AZ

stem: A Lambda function consumes an SQS standard queue with a batch size of 10. Each message triggers a charge to a customer's card through an idempotent-unaware payment API. When one message in a batch fails validation, the function throws an exception, and customers in the other nine messages are charged again on the retry. What is the MOST efficient fix?

choices.text: Replace the standard queue with a FIFO queue and set a deduplication ID on each message so that already-charged messages are dropped
Increase the queue's visibility timeout to six times the function timeout so that failed batches are not delivered again as quickly
Reduce the batch size on the event source mapping to 1 so that each invocation handles one message and a failure affects only that message
Enable ReportBatchItemFailures on the event source mapping and return the IDs of only the failed messages in the batchItemFailures list

stem: An IoT platform receives about 40,000 device events per second. Each event starts a short workflow of three steps (validate, enrich, store) that finishes in under 2 seconds, and every step is idempotent. The team wants AWS Step Functions for visual orchestration at the lowest cost. Which workflow type should they use?

choices.text: Express workflows invoked synchronously, because only synchronous runs are allowed to call other AWS services from a step
Express workflows, because they support very high start rates for short runs and are billed by request count and duration
Standard workflows started through an SQS queue, so that the queue absorbs the event rate and smooths out the execution starts
Standard workflows, because they guarantee exactly-once execution of every step and keep a detailed execution history for 90 days

stem: A retailer publishes price changes for each product. Three independent services (pricing cache, search index, and audit) must each receive every price change for a given product in the exact order it was published, process at their own pace, and retry failures separately. Which design meets these requirements?

choices.text: An Amazon SNS FIFO topic with three subscribed Amazon SQS FIFO queues, publishing each change with the product ID as the message group ID
A single Amazon SQS FIFO queue shared by all three services, publishing each change with the product ID as the message group ID for ordering
An Amazon EventBridge custom event bus with three rules, each targeting a separate Amazon SQS FIFO queue that uses the product ID as group ID
An Amazon SNS standard topic with three Amazon SQS FIFO queues subscribed to it, using the product ID as the message group ID on each queue

stem: A web application runs in an EC2 Auto Scaling group. New instances take about 12 minutes to become ready because they download a large machine-learning model and warm local caches. Traffic spikes are sudden and do not follow a daily pattern, and users see errors while new instances initialize. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Configure a predictive scaling policy so that the Auto Scaling group forecasts the load and launches instances before the spikes arrive
Create a scheduled scaling action that raises the group's minimum capacity every morning and lowers it again every evening after peak
Add a warm pool to the Auto Scaling group that keeps pre-initialized instances in the Stopped state, ready to move into service quickly
Add a lifecycle hook for launching instances so that each new instance stays in Pending:Wait until its model download has completed

stem: Orders flow through an Amazon EventBridge custom event bus to several consumers. A bug in the invoicing consumer caused it to discard events for 6 hours before it was fixed. The team must reprocess those 6 hours of order events for the invoicing consumer only, and wants the same capability for future incidents. What should the team do?

choices.text: Add an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue to the invoicing rule's target, and redrive the dead-letter queue after deploying each fix
Enable an archive on the event bus, and after a fix start a replay for the affected time window targeting only the invoicing rule
Turn on CloudTrail data events for the event bus, and resubmit the logged PutEvents calls for the time window with a script
Configure the rule's retry policy with a maximum event age of 24 hours so that failed events are delivered again automatically

stem: A Lambda function reads orders from an SQS queue and writes them to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. During a large import, the queue backlog made Lambda scale to about 900 concurrent executions, the database ran out of connections, and unrelated functions in the account were throttled. Lambda must not throttle the SQS poller. Which TWO changes meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Set reserved concurrency on the function to a low value so that Lambda rejects invocations from the poller above that limit during an import
Enable provisioned concurrency of 900 on the function so that execution environments are already initialized when the import traffic arrives
Increase the queue's visibility timeout to six times the function timeout so that messages stay hidden longer while the database is busy
Put Amazon RDS Proxy between the function and the database so that many function instances share a small pool of database connections
Set a maximum concurrency on the SQS event source mapping so that the poller never invokes more than a fixed number of function instances at once

stem: A company runs an Aurora PostgreSQL global database with its primary cluster in us-east-1 and a secondary cluster in us-west-2. For a quarterly disaster recovery exercise, the company must move the writer role to us-west-2 with no data loss, keep the global database topology intact, and later move it back. What should a solutions architect use?

choices.text: A global database failover, which promotes the secondary cluster immediately without waiting for replication to catch up with the primary
Detaching the us-west-2 cluster from the global database and promoting it to a standalone cluster that accepts writes in that Region
A global database switchover, which synchronizes the secondary with the primary before changing roles and keeps the replication topology
An Aurora Backtrack operation on the primary, followed by restoring an automated snapshot of it as a new cluster in the us-west-2 Region

stem: A Network Load Balancer spans two Availability Zones with default settings. After a partial deployment, AZ-a has 2 registered targets and AZ-b has 6. Clients resolve the NLB DNS name to both zonal IP addresses evenly. The 2 targets in AZ-a run at 100% CPU while those in AZ-b are nearly idle. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Enable cross-zone load balancing for the NLB so that each load balancer node distributes traffic across the registered targets in both zones
Increase the deregistration delay on the target group so that connections to the overloaded targets are drained more slowly and evenly
Enable sticky sessions based on source IP on the target group so that each client keeps using the same target for its later connections
Change the target group's load balancing algorithm to least outstanding requests so that busy targets automatically receive fewer new connections

stem: An application runs on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer in three Availability Zones. A networking problem in one AZ causes intermittent timeouts for requests handled there, but the target health checks keep passing. The team needs to stop sending traffic to that AZ within minutes and restore it easily afterwards. What should they do?

choices.text: Tighten the target group health check to a 2-second timeout with a threshold of 2 so the impaired zone's targets are marked unhealthy
Update the Auto Scaling group to remove the impaired AZ's subnet so that its instances terminate and capacity is launched in the other zones
Change the Route 53 alias record for the application to failover routing and point the secondary record at a static maintenance page in S3
Start a zonal shift in Amazon Application Recovery Controller for the ALB, moving traffic away from the impaired AZ for a set duration

stem: A company replicates new objects from an S3 bucket in eu-west-1 to a bucket in eu-central-1. A regulator requires that the company can show that 99.99% of new objects are copied to the second Region within 15 minutes, and operations must be alerted when an object misses that threshold. What should a solutions architect configure?

choices.text: A nightly S3 Batch Replication job that copies all new objects, with an Amazon EventBridge rule that reports failed tasks in each job
Cross-Region Replication with S3 Replication Time Control enabled, plus replication metrics and event notifications for missed thresholds
Cross-Region Replication with delete marker replication enabled, plus an AWS Config rule that checks the replication status of each object
Cross-Region Replication with S3 Transfer Acceleration enabled on both buckets, plus an S3 Storage Lens dashboard for replication status

stem: A Java application connects to an Aurora MySQL cluster by using the instance endpoint of the current writer instance. During a test failover, a replica was promoted in about 30 seconds, but the application kept failing writes for more than 10 minutes until it was restarted. Which TWO changes reduce the outage in future failovers? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a custom endpoint that contains only the current writer instance and point the application's write connections at that endpoint
Configure the JVM DNS cache TTL to a few seconds, or use the AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper, so the new writer's address is picked up quickly
Change the application's connection string to the reader endpoint, which balances connections across all instances of the cluster
Add an Aurora cross-Region replica in a second Region so that the application can switch its write connections to it during a failover
Change the application's connection string to the cluster endpoint, which always points to the instance that is currently the writer

stem: A company uses a Route 53 private hosted zone with failover routing for an internal API. The primary record points to the private IP address of an internal Network Load Balancer, and the record has a standard HTTPS health check on that IP. The health check always reports unhealthy, even when the API works. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Enable health checks on the NLB's target group and associate the target group with the failover record instead of a Route 53 health check
Allow inbound HTTPS in the NLB's security group from the Route 53 health checker IP address ranges published by AWS for each Region
Move the NLB to a public subnet and assign it an Elastic IP address so the Route 53 health checkers can reach the health check target
Create a CloudWatch alarm on the NLB's HealthyHostCount metric and associate a Route 53 health check based on that alarm with the record

stem: A DynamoDB table in us-east-1 stores customer profiles. The company must be able to restore the table as it was at any second in the past two weeks after a faulty batch job overwrites data, and must keep serving reads and writes from a second Region within seconds of a Regional outage. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add a DynamoDB Accelerator cluster in front of the table so that cached items can still be served if the table becomes unavailable
Schedule daily on-demand backups of the table with AWS Backup and copy each backup to a vault in the second Region
Convert the table to a global table with a replica in a second Region so that both Regions can serve reads and writes
Stream changes with DynamoDB Streams to a Lambda function that writes each item to a separate table in the second Region
Enable point-in-time recovery on the table so it can be restored to any second within the configured recovery period

stem: A Java Spring Boot API runs on AWS Lambda. Initialization takes about 8 seconds, and traffic is sporadic, so many requests hit cold starts. The company wants to cut cold start latency sharply without paying to keep execution environments running while the API is idle. What should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.text: Enable Lambda SnapStart on the function and invoke a published version, so new environments resume from a cached initialized snapshot
Schedule an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the function every five minutes so that one execution environment always stays warm
Increase the function's memory allocation to the maximum so that it receives more CPU and completes its initialization code faster
Configure provisioned concurrency on a published alias so that a fixed number of environments stay initialized and ready at all times

stem: A research team runs a computational fluid dynamics simulation with MPI on 128 EC2 instances. Profiling shows that scaling efficiency drops sharply beyond 64 instances because the nodes spend most of their time waiting on small, frequent messages between them. Which solution will MOST improve performance?

choices.text: Use EFA-enabled instance types in a cluster placement group and run the MPI library over libfabric so traffic bypasses the OS kernel
Use larger instance sizes with EBS-optimized throughput so that each node can read its input data and write checkpoints faster to disk
Launch the instances in a partition placement group with seven partitions so that each group of nodes sits on its own hardware rack
Launch the instances across a spread placement group and turn on ENA Express so that TCP traffic between nodes uses the SRD protocol

stem: A reporting service runs on t3.large instances launched in standard credit mode. It performs well in the morning, but every afternoon response times rise sharply. CloudWatch shows CPUCreditBalance falling to zero around noon and CPU utilization then flat at about 30%. Which TWO actions will resolve the slowdown? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Increase the Auto Scaling group's cooldown period so that new instances have longer to accumulate CPU credits before receiving traffic
Launch the instances in a cluster placement group so that network latency between the service and its database is reduced further
Move the workload to an M-family instance type such as m7i.large, which provides its full CPU performance without a credit system
Replace the gp3 root volumes with io2 volumes that have provisioned IOPS so that reports read their data from disk much more quickly
Switch the instances to unlimited credit mode so that they can keep bursting above the baseline after the earned credits are used up

stem: An e-commerce application stores orders in a DynamoDB table with partition key orderId. A new support screen must find all orders for a customer email address, sorted by order date, in single-digit milliseconds. The table already exists and holds 400 million items. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Add a local secondary index with partition key customerEmail and sort key orderDate, and query that index from the support screen
Put a DynamoDB Accelerator cluster in front of the table so that repeated lookups by customerEmail are answered from its item cache
Run a Scan on the table with a filter expression on customerEmail, and sort the returned items by orderDate in the application code
Add a global secondary index with partition key customerEmail and sort key orderDate, and query that index from the support screen

stem: A social platform stores users and follow relationships in Aurora MySQL. A new feature must suggest "people followed by people you follow" and detect fraud rings by traversing 3 to 5 levels of relationships. The recursive SQL joins take tens of seconds as data grows. Which database is the BEST fit for these queries?

choices.text: Aurora MySQL with more Aurora Replicas and a larger instance class for the writer to run the recursive joins
Amazon Neptune, storing users as vertices and follow relationships as edges, queried with Gremlin or openCypher
Amazon DocumentDB, storing each user as a document that embeds an array of the user IDs that the user follows
Amazon Redshift, loading the relationship tables nightly and running the recursive joins on its columnar engine

stem: A news site serves articles through Amazon CloudFront. The cache hit ratio is only 15%, and the origin is overloaded. The distribution uses a legacy configuration that forwards the User-Agent header and several others, all cookies, and all query strings to the origin. Articles only vary by the query string parameter lang. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Increase the default TTL and the maximum TTL of the cache behavior to one week so that edge locations keep cached objects for longer
Use a cache policy that includes only the lang query string in the cache key, and an origin request policy for values the origin needs
Add a second origin with an origin group so that CloudFront fails over to the second origin when the first returns server errors
Enable Origin Shield in the Region closest to the origin so that all edge locations fetch objects through one additional caching layer

stem: A company serves millions of requests per second through Amazon CloudFront. For every request it must rewrite legacy URLs to new paths and add security headers such as Strict-Transport-Security to responses. The logic is simple JavaScript with no network calls. Which solution provides the lowest latency and cost?

choices.text: Lambda@Edge functions on the viewer request and viewer response events that rewrite the URL and add the headers
Lambda@Edge functions on the origin request and origin response events that rewrite the URL and add the headers
CloudFront Functions on the viewer request and viewer response events that rewrite the URL and add the headers
An Application Load Balancer at the origin with listener rules that rewrite the path and insert response headers

stem: An Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer runs a Java service. Each new instance needs about 3 minutes of light traffic to warm up its JIT compiler and caches. When the group scales out, new instances pass health checks, immediately receive a full share of requests, and respond slowly or time out. What should a solutions architect configure?

choices.text: Increase the health check grace period of the Auto Scaling group to 3 minutes, so new instances are not replaced while they warm up
Enable load balancer generated cookie stickiness on the target group, so clients keep going to the warm instances they already use
Increase the deregistration delay on the target group to about 3 minutes, so existing connections are drained more slowly during scale-out
Enable slow start mode on the target group with a duration of about 3 minutes, so new targets receive a gradually increasing share of requests

stem: A log ingestion service writes about 20,000 small objects per second to one S3 bucket, all under the key prefix logs/current/. Clients receive many HTTP 503 Slow Down errors, and uploads lag behind. Which TWO actions will improve the upload throughput? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Make sure clients retry the 503 responses with exponential backoff and jitter, as the AWS SDKs do by default for throttled requests
Change the storage class of new objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering so that frequently written objects are placed on the faster tier
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket so that every upload enters AWS through the nearest CloudFront edge location first
Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket so that concurrent writes to similar keys are stored as separate versions instead of conflicts
Spread the object keys across many prefixes, for example by adding a hash-based or shard number segment near the start of each key

stem: A company is migrating a shared engineering file repository. Linux build servers must access the files over NFS, while Windows workstations joined to Active Directory must access the same files over SMB at the same time. The storage must be fully managed and span two Availability Zones. Which service meets these requirements?

choices.text: Amazon FSx for Lustre with a persistent deployment, mounted by the Linux servers and exported to the Windows clients
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server in a Multi-AZ deployment, shared over SMB to both the Windows and Linux clients
Amazon EFS with Regional storage, mounted over NFS by the Linux servers and by the Windows workstations as well
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP in a Multi-AZ deployment, serving the same volume over both the NFS and SMB protocols

services: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

stem: A SaaS company streams JSON usage events from all customers into Amazon Data Firehose, which writes them to one S3 prefix. Analysts query per-customer data with Amazon Athena, and every query scans all customers' files. The company wants events stored under prefixes such as customer_id=123/date=2026-09-01/ with no custom servers. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Configure dynamic partitioning on the Firehose stream, extracting customer_id and the date from each JSON record to build the S3 prefix
Schedule an AWS Glue crawler every hour so that it detects customer_id in the data and adds it as a partition column in the Data Catalog
Add an S3 event notification that invokes a Lambda function to copy each delivered file into per-customer prefixes and delete the original
Configure the Firehose stream's S3 buffer size to 128 MB and its buffer interval to 900 seconds so that each file holds fewer customers

stem: A Kinesis data stream with 10 shards feeds five separate consumer applications that use the GetRecords API. Writers are well below the shard write limits, but consumers regularly receive ReadProvisionedThroughputExceeded errors and lag several seconds behind. Two more consumers are planned. Each consumer needs its own read throughput and low latency. What should a solutions architect do?

choices.text: Configure every consumer to call GetRecords with a larger batch limit so that each call returns more records for each of the shards
Increase the stream's data retention period to 7 days so that lagging consumers can catch up later without losing any of the records
Register the consumers for enhanced fan-out so that each consumer receives its own 2 MB per second per shard through SubscribeToShard
Double the number of shards in the stream so that the shared read throughput and the GetRecords call limits of the stream are doubled

stem: A platform team wants application developers to create their own IAM roles for new microservices without waiting for a central team. Developers must never be able to create a role that has more permissions than an approved ceiling, even if they write an administrator policy for it. Which design enforces this?

choices.text: Give developers an identity policy that allows iam:CreateRole on all resources and rely on an IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer to alert on any overly broad role
Give developers an identity policy that allows iam:CreateRole only for role names that start with the team prefix, and review each new role manually once per week
Attach a service control policy to the developers' OU that lists the approved AWS services, and let developers create roles with any policy they like inside the OU
Give developers an identity policy that allows iam:CreateRole only when the request sets the approved permissions boundary through the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition key

stem: A company attached a service control policy to the root of its organization that denies ec2:RunInstances in every Region except eu-west-1. Instances are correctly blocked in all member accounts, but an administrator signed in to the organization's management account was still able to launch an instance in us-east-1. What explains this?

choices.text: The SCP was attached to the organization root, and SCPs attached there apply only to organizational units and never to accounts that sit directly under the root
The deny statement in the SCP takes effect only after the Region us-east-1 is explicitly disabled in the account settings of the management account
SCPs are evaluated only for IAM users, so the administrator would have been blocked only if the request had been made by an assumed IAM role instead
SCPs do not restrict the management account at all, so the administrator there is limited only by IAM policies, and workloads should run in member accounts

stem: An application team has run a set of EC2 and Lambda workloads in a production account for a year using a broad role with dozens of service permissions. Security wants to replace it with a least-privilege policy based on what the role actually calls, with as little manual analysis as possible. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation, which reviews the role's AWS CloudTrail activity for a chosen period and produces a policy containing only the actions used
Use IAM Access Analyzer to check for external access, which lists each unused action of the role and rewrites the role's policy automatically without any review
Use the IAM credential report, which lists every action the role called in the last 90 days and can be imported directly as a replacement policy
Use AWS Config with the iam-policy-no-statements-with-admin-access rule, which generates a narrower policy for every role that it flags as non-compliant

stem: A manufacturer runs a data collection service on servers in its own data centers. The service must upload files to Amazon S3, but the security policy forbids long-term IAM user access keys on those servers. The company already runs an internal public key infrastructure that issues X.509 certificates to each server. Which solution meets the requirements?

choices.text: Set up an Amazon Cognito identity pool that accepts the server certificates as an authentication provider, and return temporary credentials to each server after sign-in
Store an access key for an IAM user in AWS Secrets Manager and have each server fetch it, rotating the key every 30 days with a Lambda function
Create an IAM user for each server and require MFA through a hardware device that is installed on the server, so the keys can only be used with the second factor
Configure IAM Roles Anywhere with a trust anchor for the internal certificate authority, and let each server exchange its certificate for temporary credentials of a role

stem: A shared S3 data lake bucket is used by finance, marketing and a fraud analytics application, and each group may read only its own prefix. The bucket policy has grown to several hundred lines and hits size limits whenever a new team joins. Which change reduces the policy complexity while keeping access separated?

choices.text: Replace the bucket policy with S3 Block Public Access settings for each team, limiting each team to its prefix
Enable S3 Object Ownership set to bucket owner enforced, so that access to each prefix follows the ACL that each team sets on the objects it uploads
Create an S3 access point per team with its own policy limited to that team's prefix, and delegate access control from the bucket policy
Create one bucket per team and copy data from the data lake every night, so that each bucket needs only a short policy

stem: A developer with an IAM user in the dev account must run a deployment script that assumes an IAM role in the production account. Which TWO configurations are required for the role assumption to succeed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A copy of the developer's IAM user, created with the same name in the production account, so that the two identities can be matched
An identity policy for the developer's user in the dev account that allows sts:AssumeRole on the ARN of the production role
A VPC peering connection between the dev and production accounts, so that the security token service can be reached privately
A resource share created with AWS Resource Access Manager that includes the production role and is accepted by the dev account
A trust policy on the production role that names the dev account, or the specific dev principal, as allowed to call sts:AssumeRole

stem: A company exposes a REST API through Amazon API Gateway to its customer-facing mobile app. Customers sign in through an Amazon Cognito user pool. The company wants API Gateway to reject any request that does not carry a valid token from that user pool, without writing or hosting authorization code. Which option meets this?

choices.text: Turn on AWS IAM authorization for the methods and have the mobile app sign each request with Signature Version 4 using an access key that is embedded in the app
Create an API Gateway Lambda authorizer that downloads the user pool's public keys and validates the JWT signature and expiry in custom function code
Require an API key on every method and give each customer a key in a usage plan, so that only registered customers can invoke the API
Configure a Cognito user pool authorizer on the API methods, so that API Gateway validates the token that the client sends in the Authorization header

stem: A web application on EC2 has a server-side request forgery flaw: an attacker can make the application send HTTP requests to a URL of their choice. The attacker used it to read the instance's IAM role credentials from the link-local metadata address. The application cannot be patched immediately. Which change removes this attack path with the LEAST impact on the application?

choices.text: Add an outbound rule to the instance's security group that denies traffic to 169.254.169.254, so that the instance can no longer reach the metadata service
Move the instance to a private subnet without a route to the internet, so that the attacker cannot send the forged request from outside the VPC
Require IMDSv2 on the instance by setting the metadata option HttpTokens to required, so that a session token from a PUT request is needed to read credentials
Turn off the instance metadata service completely, and pass the role credentials to the application through environment variables in its startup script

stem: A company with 80 accounts in AWS Organizations wants every Application Load Balancer, including those in accounts created in the future, to be protected by AWS WAF with a baseline web ACL that the security team controls. Teams must not be able to detach it silently, and a single team should manage it. Which solution meets this?

choices.text: Use AWS Firewall Manager with a delegated administrator account and an AWS WAF policy that applies the baseline web ACL to all ALBs in scope
Use an AWS CloudFormation StackSet that deploys the web ACL and association to the existing accounts, and rerun it manually each time a new account is created
Use an AWS Config conformance pack that reports ALBs with no web ACL, and have each application owner attach the ACL when a finding appears
Use a service control policy that denies elasticloadbalancing:CreateLoadBalancer unless a WAF web ACL is named in the request that creates the load balancer

stem: A company builds container images in a CI pipeline, pushes them to Amazon ECR, and runs them on ECS with AWS Fargate. Security wants each image scanned for known software vulnerabilities when it is pushed and rescanned when new vulnerabilities are published, with findings sent to one central place. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon Inspector with enhanced scanning for ECR, which scans on push and rescans as new CVEs appear, with findings sent to Security Hub
AWS Config with a managed rule for ECR image scanning, which patches the vulnerable libraries in each stored image after the scan completes
Amazon GuardDuty with Runtime Monitoring turned on, which reports known CVEs for packages in each image
Amazon Macie with a scan job on the ECR repository, which lists the operating system and library CVEs found in each image layer

stem: Security analysts found that malware on several EC2 instances resolves attacker-controlled domain names, using DNS queries to carry stolen data out of the VPC. Outbound web traffic is already filtered. The company needs to block resolution of known malicious domains and log such queries from all VPCs. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Network Firewall with a stateful domain list rule group, deployed in each VPC and applied to the DNS queries that instances send to the Route 53 Resolver, blocking the malicious domains
AWS WAF web ACLs associated with each VPC, using AWS managed rule groups that block requests to domains flagged by AWS threat intelligence and log every matching DNS query
Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall with AWS managed domain lists and custom lists, associated with the VPCs and configured to block and log matching queries
Network ACLs on every subnet with outbound deny rules for the IP addresses of the malicious domains, kept up to date by a scheduled Lambda function that reads a threat intelligence feed

stem: A security team runs AWS Security Hub in 40 accounts and three Regions. Analysts must see all findings in one console and enable Security Hub in new accounts automatically. Which TWO actions set this up? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Turn on AWS CloudTrail in every account, because Security Hub reads only management events from CloudTrail to produce its findings
Export findings from each account to an S3 bucket every hour, and query the objects with Athena from the security account
Create an IAM user in each member account, and have the analysts sign in to each of them to review its Security Hub findings
Designate a delegated administrator account for Security Hub in AWS Organizations and enable automatic enrollment of new member accounts
Configure cross-Region aggregation in the administrator account, choosing one aggregation Region and linking the other two Regions so that their findings appear there

stem: A photo sharing service lets customers upload files directly to an S3 bucket. The company must detect malware in each newly uploaded object before other systems process it, prefers a managed service over running scanning servers, and wants results as object tags for downstream automation. Which solution fits?

choices.text: An EC2 Auto Scaling group running an open source antivirus engine that polls the bucket every hour, and copies the clean objects to a second bucket
Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection for Amazon S3, enabled for the bucket, which scans new objects and tags each one with the scan result
Amazon Macie with an automated discovery job on the bucket, which scans new objects for malware signatures and tags each infected object
Amazon Inspector with S3 scanning turned on, which checks each object for known CVEs and marks the infected objects as unsafe

stem: A team has 300 application settings for a fleet of Lambda functions, including 20 that are passwords or API tokens for third-party services that never need automated rotation. Values must be encrypted with a KMS key, changed without redeploying code, and the company wants the lowest cost. Which option fits?

choices.text: Store every value as a separate secret in AWS Secrets Manager, and turn on automatic rotation for all secrets so that values are changed regularly
Store every value in the Lambda function environment variables, and use the default Lambda encryption that AWS manages for the variables
Store every value in a JSON file in an S3 bucket, encrypted with SSE-S3, and have each function download the file at every cold start
Store every value as a standard tier SecureString parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, encrypted with a customer managed KMS key

stem: A company must rotate its KMS keys every 180 days to meet an internal policy. Its applications use a customer managed symmetric key through an alias, and existing S3 objects and EBS snapshots must stay readable without being re-encrypted or reconfigured. Which approach meets this?

choices.text: Run a Lambda function that calls ReEncrypt on every object protected by the key each 180 days, storing the new ciphertext
Import the company's own key material into the key and rely on automatic rotation to replace the imported material with new material every 180 days
Enable automatic rotation on the customer managed key with a 180 day period, so the key ID and alias stay the same and older key material is kept
Create a new key every 180 days, repoint the alias to it, and re-encrypt existing objects and snapshots before deleting the old key

stem: A company serves private product images from an Amazon S3 bucket through an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The objects are encrypted with SSE-KMS using a customer managed key. Requests that go straight to the S3 URL must be denied, and only this one distribution may read the objects. Which configuration meets this?

choices.text: Create an origin access identity for the S3 origin, allow its canonical user in the bucket policy, and allow that identity to call kms:Decrypt on the customer managed key through the key policy statement

Create an origin access control for the S3 origin, allow the cloudfront.amazonaws.com principal in the bucket policy with an aws:SourceArn condition for this distribution, and allow kms:Decrypt in the key policy

Keep the bucket readable through a bucket policy that allows GetObject only from the published CloudFront IP address ranges, and refresh the policy through a scheduled job whenever AWS changes those ranges

Enable static website hosting on the bucket with public read access, and have CloudFront send a secret Referer header that the bucket policy checks before it allows any GetObject request from the distribution

stem: A security policy requires that connections to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 14 instance use TLS. A penetration test shows that a client can still connect with a plain, unencrypted session, although storage encryption is enabled and the security group allows only the application subnet. What should the team do?

choices.text: Set the rds.force_ssl parameter to 1 in the instance's custom DB parameter group, so that the server rejects connections that do not use TLS
Move the DB instance into a private subnet, so that unencrypted sessions from inside the VPC are dropped by the network
Re-create the DB instance from an encrypted snapshot copy that uses a customer managed key, which also requires TLS for every client session
Restrict the security group so that port 5432 is open only to the application subnet and to the bastion host that the testers used

stem: A company has an Amazon EFS file system, created without encryption, that stores customer documents for Linux application servers. A new policy requires encryption of the data at rest and in transit. Which TWO actions meet the policy? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a new file system with encryption at rest turned on, and copy the data into it by using AWS DataSync
Edit the existing file system and turn on encryption at rest, so that EFS re-encrypts the stored data in the background
Restrict the mount target security group to accept NFS traffic on port 2049 only from the application servers' security group
Move the documents to an Amazon EBS volume that is attached to a single instance, and take snapshots of the volume every day
Mount the file system with the amazon-efs-utils mount helper and the tls option, so that NFS traffic is encrypted with TLS

stem: A DynamoDB table stores payment records. Compliance says the company must be able to disable the encryption key to render the data unreadable in an emergency, and must see every use of that key in AWS CloudTrail. The table currently uses the default encryption. Which change meets the requirements?

choices.text: Enable client-side encryption of the sensitive attributes and store the encryption keys in a private table of the same DynamoDB account
Switch the table encryption to a customer managed KMS key, which the company can disable and whose use appears in CloudTrail
Switch the table to the AWS managed key aws/dynamodb, which the company can disable at any time and whose key policy it can edit
Keep the default encryption with an AWS owned key, which the company can disable from the DynamoDB console and which logs each use in CloudTrail

stem: An administrator scheduled deletion of a customer managed KMS key that was believed to be unused. Two days later, applications that read S3 objects encrypted with that key start failing with KMSInvalidStateException errors. The key had a 30-day waiting period. What is the correct recovery?

choices.text: Restore the key from the automatic KMS backup that is kept for the waiting period, then reimport its key material
Open a support case to request an extension of the waiting period, and wait until the key is fully deleted to restore it
Cancel the scheduled key deletion, and then enable the key, since the key returns in a disabled state after cancellation
Create a new KMS key with the same alias name, and the applications will decrypt the existing objects with the new key
